credentials.description: API key from the Wave Business portal (sent as Authorization: Bearer); it is tied to a real wallet — Wave documents no sandbox

example_prompt: Add Wave payouts to my disbursement flow.

receive_amount.description: Amount the recipient receives, as a string, without decimals. e.g. "5000".

mobile.description: Recipient's phone number in E.164 format. e.g. "+221700000000".

name.description: Recipient's name (max 255 chars). Used for verification if national_id is also provided.

national_id.description: Recipient's national ID document number (max 255 chars). Optional.

client_reference.description: Internal reference (max 255 chars) to correlate the payout with your system.

payment_reason.description: Payment reason visible to the recipient (max 40 chars).

aggregated_merchant_id.description: Aggregated merchant ID. Required for aggregators that have enabled the Aggregated Merchants API.

id.description: Unique payout identifier (prefix "pt-", max 20 chars). Store it to be able to do a reversal or track the status via get_payout.

status.description: Payout state. 'processing' means the result is not final yet. 'reversed' indicates that the payout was cancelled via POST /v1/payout/{id}/reverse.

code.description: Error code. e.g. insufficient-funds, recipient-account-blocked, idempotency-mismatch.

details.description: Validation details returned on request-validation-error. Each entry contains loc (field location), msg (message), type (error type). Can be null or absent (measured on 2026-10-24 on 401 errors) — check before iterating.

gotchas: Every POST /v1/payout request must include a unique Idempotency-Key header (UUID v4 recommended, max 255 chars). Without this key, a retry after a network error can create a duplicate payout.

If the payout returns status 'processing', do not mark it as failed — treat it as pending and monitor it via GET /v1/payout/{id}. Marking it as failed too early can push the user to retry, causing a duplicate.
On a 5xx error, timeout or interrupted connection: retry with the SAME Idempotency-Key and exponential backoff. Wave guarantees idempotency.
On an 'idempotency-mismatch' error (409): the same Idempotency-Key was used with a different body. Generate a new key and retry.
Reversing a payout is limited to 3 days after creation. After that period, POST /v1/payout/{id}/reverse returns an error.
receive_amount is a string without decimals for XOF — send "5000", not 5000 or "5000.00".

If the API key was created with request signing (optional Business Portal setting), every call must carry Wave-Signature: t={timestamp},v1={HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + raw body)} computed with the signing secret (format wave_sn_AKS_…, shown only once) — empty body for a GET. Without it: 401 missing-signature; other codes: invalid-signature, invalid-signature-format, invalid-signature-timestamp, expired-signature-timestamp (timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past or more than 30 seconds in the future). The setting is permanent for a key: to drop it, revoke the key and create another one.

[MUST TELL USER] The API IP whitelist turns on as soon as the first address is added in the Business Portal (Developer section) and can no longer be turned off from the portal — you have to go through your Wave account manager. Calls from an unlisted IP get 403 ip-not-allowed: on hosting without a fixed outbound IP (serverless functions, most PaaS), do not add any IP before you have a fixed egress.
